key_insight: T3D uses the model's own multi-step generative trajectories to self-distill a few-step decoder, combined with a direct discriminative optimization objective, enabling diffusion LLMs to generate high-quality text with far fewer refinement steps.
problem_solved: Diffusion LLMs can decode tokens in parallel but require many refinement steps for good quality; aggressively reducing steps degrades generation. T3D addresses how to retain high-quality outputs while drastically cutting the number of refinement steps.
method: Trajectory self-distillation: collect the model's multi-step generative trajectories and use them as targets to train a few-step student decoder.
Direct discriminative optimization: apply a discriminative loss to directly encourage the student to prefer higher-quality trajectory states and correct errors from aggressive step reduction.
Jointly align parallel-token diffusion decoding with distilled trajectories so the student learns to reproduce the teacher's final-quality outputs in far fewer steps.
impact: Enables practical, low-latency deployment of diffusion-based language models by preserving generation quality while reducing inference steps — important for real-time systems and cost-efficient large-model serving.

paper_title: T3D: Few-Step Diffusion Language Models via Trajectory Self-Distillation with Direct Discriminative Optimization
paper_authors: Tunyu Zhang, Xinxi Zhang, Ligong Han, Haizhou Shi, Xiaoxiao He
